title: The Quiet Push
briefing.company: Mercadito is a marketplace: thousands of small shops, one checkout. Orders go from the storefront to checkout-api, which calls the cart, the payments database and an external payment gateway that someone else runs.
briefing.role: You're on call for checkout this week. It's Thursday. Nobody else is awake, which is the whole point of you.
change.deployCart: cart-api 3.8.1: dependency bumps, no behavior change
change.promoFlag: promo banner on for the morning campaign
change.timeout: align payment timeout with the provider's SLA doc (8s)
runbook.checkoutLatency.title: Checkout latency is high
runbook.checkoutLatency.body:
Checkout latency is the sum of its dependencies. Before touching anything, find out which one got slower and when.

First, look at what changed: deploys, config pushes and flags in the last hours. Most nights, the answer is in that list.

Then split the time: server latency for checkout-api against client latency for each call it makes. The call that grew is the suspect. Its timeouts and retries decide how long a customer waits.

Restarting checkout-api clears in-flight requests and nothing else. Use it only if you know why.
runbook.paymentGw.title: payment-gw (external provider)
runbook.paymentGw.body:
payment-gw is run by an outside provider. We see it only through our own client metrics and spans: there are no server-side signals.

Every night between 02:30 and 05:00 the provider runs settlement. During that window a few percent of authorize calls hang for nine seconds or more. They don't fail; they just never answer in time.

The provider recommends a client timeout of 1 s or less with one retry. A short timeout turns a hung call into a fast retry that almost always succeeds.

A word on retries: a client that gave up waiting does not know the provider didn't charge the card. A safe retry needs an idempotency key, a fixed number of attempts and a total time budget. Without them, a short timeout turns a slow night into double charges, or into more load on a provider that is already struggling.
mitigation.revert-cfg-413.title: Roll back checkout-api config v413 → v412
mitigation.revert-cfg-413.what: Restores payment.client.timeout_ms to its previous value on every instance.
mitigation.restart-checkout.title: Restart checkout-api
mitigation.restart-checkout.what: Fresh processes, same config. Drops in-flight requests for about a minute.
mitigation.restart-checkout.doing: Restarting checkout-api, one instance at a time…
mitigation.scale-checkout.title: Scale checkout-api from 4 to 8 instances
mitigation.scale-checkout.what: More capacity. Helps if the problem is load.
prompt.lucia.ask: The morning team in Bogotá is asking why checkout feels slow. Are we losing orders? What do I tell them?
factor.timeoutRaised: A config change raised the payment client timeout from 800 ms to 8 s.
factor.gwSlowTail: During its nightly settlement window, the payment gateway leaves about 7% of calls hanging.
factor.unguardedConfig: Config changes reach every instance at once, with no canary and no bounds check.
distractor.cartDeploy: Tonight's cart-api deploy introduced a regression.
distractor.promoBanner: The promo banner flag added load to the storefront.
chain.unguarded: Config pushes skip canaries and bounds checks
chain.change: 03:03 · config v413: payment timeout 800 ms → 8 s
chain.settlement: payment-gw settlement window: ~7% of calls hang
chain.waiting: Hung calls now wait 8 s before the retry, not 0.8 s
chain.customers: Customers wait 8 s or more to pay; some give up
debrief.chainNote: The short timeout used to hide the gateway's bad nights: a hung call failed fast and the retry went through. Raising it turned a hidden condition into a visible one. The person who pushed it read a real document and made a reasonable change; the system let it reach every instance at once.
